_comment: Which benchmark reports belong together. Gemini's free-tier daily cap forced the benchmark to be run in fragments across many sessions, so no single report holds the full picture -- but runs from different judge prompt versions must never be pooled, since that would average away the exact signal the prompt change was made to test. This file makes that grouping reviewable data rather than a filename-prefix guess hidden in JavaScript. benchmark.html merges within an era and refuses to merge across. Each era also records the judge that produced it. The report files predate run_benchmark.py stamping the provider on every run, so for these the judge comes from the project's own records (the Gemini free-tier cap documented in the README is what forced them into fragments) rather than from the data. Reports written from now on carry a "judges" array and a "mixed_judges" flag, and benchmark.html prefers those over this field.

eras.label: PASS 3 added (support checks)
eras.prompt: Adds a third pass over the same extracted claims: (a) unsupported commitment -- a claim settles on one of several surfaced options with nothing justifying the choice, gated on whether the options are interchangeable for the task; (b) dropped caveat -- a claim repeats a value while leaving behind a qualifier attached to it at its source.
eras.description: Built to close the gap the cross-model run exposed: two traces failing on every model because their failures are not contradictions. 30/30 correct, zero false positives. Read with care -- PASS 3 was developed against this benchmark across three iterations, so this run is partly in-sample and is not an independent test of the change. The genuinely held-out check is the real trace, which still lands on step 15.

eras.label: After the structural fix
eras.prompt: Judge prompt requires a "claims" array emitted before the verdict, forcing claim extraction to be a visible output rather than an internal instruction.
eras.description: The regression check: does requiring claim extraction, which fixed the real-trace miss, cost anything on the synthetic ground-truth set?
eras.judge_source: project records, not stamped in the report

eras.label: Structural fix, judged by Groq gpt-oss-120b
eras.prompt: Identical to the structural-fix prompt above. Only the judge model differs.
eras.description: The same prompt and the same labels, run against a different model -- so this measures how much of the claims-extraction contract is carried by the prompt rather than by Gemini specifically. It is also the only complete run in this repo: 30 of 30 calls finished, nothing errored, every trace sampled 3 times. Its 80% is therefore a more trustworthy number than the 90% above, which rests on 21 completed calls out of 63 attempted, unevenly spread across traces by whenever the free tier let a call through. Do not read the two percentages as a like-for-like comparison.

eras.label: Before the structural fix
eras.prompt: Original judge prompt, plus a later prose-only revision telling the judge contradictions can be prose-buried. Neither version required claims as output.
eras.description: A PARTIAL view, not the headline pre-fix number. These two reports cover only 5 of the 10 traces -- the ones still outstanding when they were run -- and they are weighted toward the hard cases, so the accuracy shown here is lower than the README's 40/45 (89%). That figure also counts runs recorded in output/consistency_*.json and in sessions that produced no benchmark report at all; those files carry no ground-truth label or per-run correctness, so they cannot be merged in here without re-scoring them.
eras.judge_source: project records, not stamped in the report

eras.label: Pre-bugfix scorer (do not trust the numbers)
eras.description: The first benchmark run, scored before judge.py distinguished JudgeUnavailableError from 'found nothing'. A failed API call was counted as the judge examining a trace and finding no failure -- which inflated false negatives and, on the clean traces, faked correct answers by coincidence. Kept deliberately: it is the recorded evidence of the silent-failure bug this project exists to catch, not a result.
